{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW self-contained HTML5 file `effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html`: a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating cube rendered with a software 3D pipeline on Canvas 2D only (no WebGL, no external libraries, no external assets). All code inline in one <script> block. English comments.

=== PAGE / STYLE ===
- <!DOCTYPE html>, <meta charset>, viewport, title "Gouraud-Shaded Cube — Canvas 2D".
- Dark page background (#0b0e14 with a subtle radial gradient), body margin 0, overflow hidden.
- <canvas> fills the window (position fixed, inset 0, width/height 100vw/100vh, display block).
- HUD overlay top-left: fixed, monospace font (e.g. "Consolas, monospace"), semi-transparent dark rounded box, contains: big FPS number (e.g. "60 FPS") and a status line showing "wireframe: OFF · paused: NO".
- Bottom-center hint line (fixed, dim text): "W — wireframe    P — pause".

=== 3D DATA ===
- 8 cube vertices at ±1.1 (half-extent 1.1).
- 6 faces as quads (4 vertex indices each), each with its own base RGB color, e.g.: +x tomato (255,99,71), -x sea green (60,179,113), +y amber (255,205,84), -y periwinkle (108,122,224), +z pink (240,98,146), -z light blue (79,195,247). Winding of each face consistent (outward normals via cross product).
- At init: compute each face unit normal from its quad, and per-VERTEX unit normals as the normalized sum of the 3 adjacent face normals (true Gouraud vertex normals).

=== PIPELINE (per frame) ===
1. Rotation: build a 3x3 rotation matrix R = Rz*Ry*Rx from angles that advance with simulation time (e.g. rx = 0.65*t, ry = 1.05*t, rz = 0.35*t).
2. Transform the 8 vertices: p = R·v, then translate camera-space depth: pz = p.z + CAM_DIST (CAM_DIST = 4, camera at origin looking down +z).
3. Rotate the 6 face normals and the 8 vertex normals by R.
4. Perspective projection: focal = 1.30 * min(W,H); sx = W/2 + x*focal/pz; sy = H/2 - y*focal/pz. Store screen x,y plus pz.
5. Moving point light: light position orbits the cube in camera space, e.g. L = [2.9*sin(1.25t), 1.9*sin(0.85t)+0.5, 4 + 2.5*cos(1.0t)].
6. Per-vertex Lambert lighting (done at the 8 cube vertices): litColor[i] = baseColorVertex? — use per-face colors: for each face, for its 4 vertices compute Ldir = normalize(L - worldVertexPos) where worldVertexPos = rotated vertex + [0,0,CAM_DIST]; diffuse = max(0, dot(rotatedVertexNormal, Ldir)); shade = clamp(ambient + diffuse*(1-ambient), 0, 1) with ambient = 0.18; vertex lit RGB = face base RGB * shade. (A vertex shared by faces gets a lit value per face — that is fine and keeps face colors distinct.)
7. Backface culling: face center c = average of rotated translated vertices; face visible iff dot(rotatedNormal, -c) > 0. Only visible faces are rasterized.
8. Each visible quad is split into 2 triangles: (v0,v1,v2) and (v0,v2,v3).

=== RASTERIZER (Gouraud) ===
- Keep an ImageData whose 32-bit view (Uint32Array, little-endian ABGR) is the framebuffer, plus a Float32Array depth buffer sized W*H.
- Each shaded frame: data32.fill(0xff140e1a-ish background ABGR) and depth.fill(1e9); then putImageData once at the end of the frame.
- Per triangle: bounding box clamped to screen; for each pixel center (x+0.5, y+0.5) compute barycentric coordinates via edge functions w0=edge(b,c,p), w1=edge(c,a,p), w2=edge(a,b,p) with edge(a,b,p) = (b.x-a.x)*(p.y-a.y) - (b.y-a.y)*(p.x-a.x); area = edge(a,b,c); if |area| < eps skip; if area < 0 swap vertices b/c (and weights) so weights are positive. Inside test: all weights >= 0.
- Interpolate per-vertex lit RGB and depth linearly in screen space (classic Gouraud): value = (w0*va + w1*vb + w2*vc)/area. Depth test: z <= depth[idx] → write pixel (data32[idx] = 0xff000000 | (b<<16) | (g<<8) | r with r,g,b clamped to 0..255 ints) and store z. Inclusive depth test avoids cracks on shared edges.

=== WIREFRAME MODE ===
- When wireframe is ON: skip the framebuffer; clear canvas with ctx.fillRect background; draw all 6 face outlines as projected line loops (ctx.beginPath per face, moveTo/lineTo projected vertices, closePath), stroke color = the face's base color at full brightness, lineWidth 1.5. Draw light marker too.

=== LIGHT MARKER ===
- After drawing (both modes): if light z > 0.2, project the light position and draw a small radial-gradient glow dot (radius ~10px scaled by focal/pz) in warm yellow to visualize the moving light.

=== HUD / FPS ===
- FPS: exponential moving average fps = fps*0.9 + (1/dt)*0.1 (guard dt>0, clamp dt to 0.1 s). Update HUD text each frame: fpsEl.textContent = Math.round(fps) + " FPS"; status line shows wireframe and paused state.
- requestAnimationFrame main loop; simulation time only advances when not paused (pause freezes rotation and light, rendering continues).

=== INPUT ===
- keydown: 'w'/'W' toggles wireframe, 'p'/'P' toggles pause. Update the HUD status immediately.

=== MISC ===
- resize handler: canvas.width = innerWidth, canvas.height = innerHeight; reallocate ImageData/data32/depth buffers.
- Code organized in small functions with section comments: DATA, PIPELINE, LIGHTING, RASTERIZER, RENDER, LOOP, INPUT. No console errors; no unused variables; works when opened directly from disk (file://)."}
